![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14182820/assets/70d961102240b0c48132baca8db0b77ed80ff8e0d3b7296bd5c727ab2f97dfd3.png)

The perimeter of the above triangle is $18+9\sqrt{2}.$ Find the measure of each leg.
question.worked_solution:
Because the triangle is isosceles, the legs must have the same length. Let $a$ be the length of each leg. So, we have

$$
AB=BC=a.
$$

Moreover, because the triangle is a *right* isosceles triangle, the hypotenuse must be equal to $\sqrt{2}$ times the length of a leg. Therefore,

$$
AC=AB\cdot \sqrt{2}=a\sqrt{2}.
$$

Finally, since the perimeter is $p=18+9\sqrt{2},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =AB+BC+AC \\ 18+9\sqrt{2} & =a+a+a\sqrt{2} \\ 9(2+\sqrt{2}) & =2a+a\sqrt{2} \\ 9(2+\sqrt{2}) & =(2+\sqrt{2})a \\ 9\cancel{(2+\sqrt{2})} & =\cancel{(2+\sqrt{2})}a \\ 9 & =a.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the measure of a leg is $9.$
